answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a costly, decaying work bond: to join, an agent locks a stake and must complete verified useful work over time, like a river carving a channel, before earning full trading rights. A single fake identity is cheap, but a plume of thousands, each needing its own stake and sustained work, becomes ruinously expensive. If one misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its reputation falls to its nadir, so attackers pay in full for every identity while honest agents earn standing once.
